formula: midpoint of a sourced range the source printed without a central value
rationale: A source that prints only a range (a lifetime of 10-20 years) gives no central value, and the extraction layer never invents one (design s5). At the archetype level the model needs a point, so the midpoint stands in, graded estimated: the range is sourced, the point within it is a convention. The row keeps its sources and n.

formula: whole Bayer refinery less the gas suspension calciner, per t alumina (capex, fixed O&M)
rationale: The alumina end use is split into digestion and calcination steps (Brad 2026-10-28). The current, reliable energy and emissions figures (IAI 2025, Australian refineries 2020, DOE 2017) are for whole refineries, now on the reference archetype refinery_alumina; the digestion step takes them less the gas calciner (MPP 2023 and the calciner's own sources), where the step has no figure of its own (the Alcoa 2022 per-refinery powerhouse emissions are digestion-only and stay sourced). A carrier the calciner does not use is taken whole. Graded estimated: the two come from different sources. Energy and combustion emissions no longer come from this rule (node alignment NF01, rule 1, Brad 2026-11-05): the refinery fuel that raises digestion steam is bought as steam from the sector steam node; digester_bayer carries steam = (whole refinery fuel less calciner fuel) x 82% boiler efficiency, in records/fill/fill-judgement.csv.

formula: 100 / efficiency, replacing a sourced total from one or two examples; carriers in the total scaled to it
rationale: On an energy-service archetype measured per GJ of output, energy use is 100 / efficiency by definition. On these five the total came from one or two examples (a DOE worked example at 70% on the fuel-fired boiler; Element Energy's 92% LHV table figure on the direct heater; Pardo's current-EU by-product-gas plant on the condensing turbine) while the efficiency pools 15-70 examples, and the two disagreed by 15-30%. The efficiency-based total agrees with the archetypes' own carrier pools (fuel-fired boiler natural gas median 1.25 against 1.23; condensing turbine Pardo BAT and NRCan 2.71-2.73). The sourced total is kept as target as-sourced.

formula: 100 / efficiency
rationale: An energy-service archetype measured per GJ of output uses 100/efficiency GJ of energy per GJ of output: the two are one quantity stated two ways. NARROWED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check S105): not on lighting, cooling towers or ventilation units, whose energy figure is an index or a recovery effectiveness, nor on liquefaction trains or incinerators, whose energy figure is a parasitic or auxiliary load; and an efficiency above 100% is written only on heat-moving equipment (heat pumps, chillers, vapour recompression). Not on the conversion archetypes of records/reference/feedstock.csv (ruling 2026-10-13): their energy use leaves out the feed in the product, so it is no longer 100/efficiency.

formula: 100 / efficiency - energy in the product (records/reference/feedstock.csv)
rationale: On a conversion archetype per GJ of product the efficiency counts the feed as an input: 100/efficiency GJ in per GJ out, of which the energy in the product is feedstock-consumption and the rest is burned as energy (ruling 2026-10-13 item 4). Fills the energy use where no example gives one (sanity-check 2026-10-23, OG003).

formula: 100 / heat efficiency (the efficiency row with target heat, else efficiency-chp less electric efficiency)
rationale: A CHP archetype's energy use is per GJ of heat, its product, with electricity a co-product (IEAGHG 2007: 'fuel input 3.9 MW per 2.0 MWth heat output'); where no source gives it, it is 100 / the heat efficiency (sanity-check run 2026-10-24, P-C6: biomass CHP had none). Graded estimated, since the total and electric efficiencies can come from different examples; heat efficiency outside 15-80% is not used. Not on anaerobic-digester_chp, whose efficiencies are the engine's on biogas while its carriers are the digester's feed.

formula: 100 / (energy use + energy in the product (records/reference/feedstock.csv))
rationale: The inverse of id-sec-from-efficiency-net-feed: on a conversion archetype the feed whose energy ends in the product is feedstock-consumption, so the efficiency is 100 over energy use plus that energy (sanity-check run 2026-10-24, P-C8). Not where the energy use itself came from the efficiency. On methane pyrolysis the efficiency is to hydrogen only: the carbon co-product's energy counts as energy used (feedstock.csv).

formula: 100 / specific-energy-consumption
rationale: The same identity read the other way. OFF 2026-09-30: on its first run it gave a 7% motor efficiency, 154% for the methane reformer (range to 10,700%) and 183% for a simple-cycle turbine. A pooled specific-energy-consumption with no carrier is not reliably the TOTAL input per GJ of output (UKERC measure rows, examples that give only one carrier), so its inverse is not an efficiency. Turn on per archetype only after checking what the SEC counts. RE-ENABLED 2026-10-09 with a carrier condition: only on GJ-product archetypes that are not CHP, whose all-carrier total agrees with its carrier split (pipeline/carriers.py), and only where the result lies between 10% and 800% (heat pumps reach several hundred per cent). The failures of 2026-09-30 came from totals that were partial or on another scope; the split now makes a total checkable. NARROWED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check S105): not on lighting, cooling towers or ventilation units, whose energy figure is an index or a recovery effectiveness, nor on liquefaction trains or incinerators, whose energy figure is a parasitic or auxiliary load; and an efficiency above 100% is written only on heat-moving equipment (heat pumps, chillers, vapour recompression). Not on the conversion archetypes of records/reference/feedstock.csv (ruling 2026-10-13): their energy use leaves out the feed in the product, so it is no longer 100/efficiency.

formula: the archetype lists one carrier: that carrier = the unnamed fuel row where there is one, else the all-carrier total
rationale: Where an archetype uses one energy carrier (its carriers list) and the sources give its energy use without naming the carrier, all of it is that carrier, by definition. Lets the combustion CO2 identity and the CIMS service request by carrier follow. Not on an efficiency variant whose host splits its energy over two or more carriers: that variant takes the host's mix (est-variant-host-split; sanity-check 2026-10-23 S135/PB004).

formula: each carrier = the host's carrier x (the variant's total / the host's total)
inputs: specific-energy-consumption of the variant (total) and of its host (records/fill/host-archetype.csv) by carrier
rationale: An efficiency variant uses less of the same energy mix as the plant it improves; a judgement that rewrote the mix made efficient variants dirtier than their hosts (blast-furnace_efficiency-moderate 1.30 t CO2/t against 0.79; sanity-check 2026-10-11 IS009, IS010). Runs before the carrier judgements and the CO2 identity, so a guessed split is used only where the host has none.

formula: the host's combustion CO2 x (the variant's total energy use / the host's)
inputs: emissions-combustion co2 of the host; specific-energy-consumption of the variant and the host
rationale: An efficiency variant burns less of the same mix, so its combustion CO2 is the host's scaled by the energy saving. Taken from the host's own value, not rebuilt from carriers, because a host's sourced combustion CO2 can differ from its carriers x emission factors (a blast furnace's coke is partly reductant and leaves as top gas). Runs before id-combustion-co2-from-fuel (sanity-check 2026-10-11 IS009).

formula: feedstock-consumption (the carrier in records/reference/feedstock.csv) = the energy the product holds, GJ HHV per product unit
rationale: A conversion archetype's product holds the energy of its feed (hydrogen from gas, ammonia, methanol, fuels from biomass or oil), and the energy use leaves that part out (ruling 2026-10-13). Where no source gives the feed separately, it is at least the product's energy; written so the feed is requested and priced.

formula: sum over fossil carriers of specific-energy-consumption(carrier) x CO2 emission factor(carrier)
rationale: Fuel burned times its carbon content. Only where the archetype names the fossil carrier its energy use is in (a carrier-specific specific-energy-consumption), and never where fuel may also be a feedstock (reformers, gasifiers, reactors) or where process emissions are recorded, since a feedstock share would then be counted twice or in the wrong column. Scope 1: electricity and biomass carry no factor. CHANGED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check run, P-C1; Fable review): no longer skipped where process CO2 is recorded, nor on steam reformers and reactors: energy use is net of feedstock since 2026-10-13, so their fuel rows are fuel burned. Still not on gasifiers and autothermal reformers, whose net energy use includes feed oxidised in the process stream (their CO2 leaves through acid-gas removal, not a stack), nor on shaft-furnace_electrolytic-hydrogen (its coal is EAF charge carbon inside the process CO2). On the archetypes this change newly reaches (a process-CO2 row, a steam reformer or reactor; never a capture variant or capture plant, whose totals are net of capture), it is not written where fuel CO2 plus process CO2 exceeds a sourced emissions-total CO2 by 10% or the total is 0, nor from zero-valued fuel rows; both are listed in the build log. Archetypes it reached before keep their row, and an exceedance there is listed in the build log for review. Not on pneumatic-device_gas-driven or _low-bleed (2026-10-24, sanity-check run P-D3): their natural-gas row is motive gas the devices vent, not burn; its methane is their emissions-process CH4.

formula: CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265 + SF6 x 23,500 + CF4 x 6,630 + C2F6 x 11,100 (IPCC AR5 100-year GWPs)
rationale: CO2-eq on one basis: the AR5 100-year GWPs Canada's National Inventory Report uses (ruling 2026-10-14). Written only where a non-CO2 gas is known and no CO2-eq is; a gas the archetype emits but no source gives is missing from the sum.

formula: CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265 + SF6 x 23,500 + CF4 x 6,630 + C2F6 x 11,100 (IPCC AR5 100-year GWPs)
rationale: CO2-eq on one basis: the AR5 100-year GWPs Canada's National Inventory Report uses (ruling 2026-10-14). Written only where a non-CO2 gas is known and no CO2-eq is; a gas the archetype emits but no source gives is missing from the sum.

formula: CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265 + SF6 x 23,500 + CF4 x 6,630 + C2F6 x 11,100 (IPCC AR5 100-year GWPs)
rationale: CO2-eq on one basis: the AR5 100-year GWPs Canada's National Inventory Report uses (ruling 2026-10-14). Written only where a non-CO2 gas is known and no CO2-eq is; a gas the archetype emits but no source gives is missing from the sum.

formula: cost per t of the one gas abated / its AR5 100-year GWP
rationale: CO2-eq on one basis: the AR5 100-year GWPs Canada's National Inventory Report uses (ruling 2026-10-14). Written only where a non-CO2 gas is known and no CO2-eq is; a gas the archetype emits but no source gives is missing from the sum.

formula: emissions-combustion (CO2) / CO2 emission factor of the archetype's one fossil carrier
rationale: The inverse of id-combustion-co2-from-fuel: where a source gives the combustion CO2 of an archetype that burns one fossil carrier and nothing gives its energy use, the fuel burned is the CO2 over the carrier's carbon content (ECCC NIR factors on HHV). Written as the total and as that carrier. Not where process emissions are recorded (the CO2 would not all be fuel).

formula: combustion CO2 = 0: every carrier the archetype lists is non-combustible (electricity, steam, hydrogen, geothermal, solar, nuclear, waste heat, ammonia) or biogenic (biomass, biogas, black liquor, landfill gas: their CO2 is not fossil CO2)
rationale: An archetype that burns nothing with carbon in it emits no combustion CO2 on site; its emissions are in the electricity or steam it buys, which the model prices. Written only where no energy-use row names a combustible carrier. NOT on reactor_fluid-coking (2026-10-24, sanity-check run P-C2): its carriers list names steam and electricity, but the coke burner supplies the reactor's heat, so its combustion CO2 is not 0. Geothermal wells excluded 2026-10-28: their non-condensable-gas CO2 is not from fuel, and a zero would contradict the CO2-eq the sources give.

formula: emissions-combustion + emissions-process, same species; also replaces a sourced total more than 10% below the parts
rationale: Total scope-1 emissions are combustion plus process emissions; filled only where both are recorded for the same species and the total is not. BELOW PARTS 2026-10-28 (Brad, IS009/MCF011): a sourced total more than 10% below its own combustion + process is replaced by the parts, where the parts are sourced, identities or estimates; not on a total net of capture (a captured row), and not on smelting-vessel_smelting-reduction (the total is net of the export gas, batch C IS008, while Hu's combustion is gross of it).

formula: opex-total - opex-fixed
rationale: Where a source gives an all-in operating cost and a fixed O&M beside it, the difference is the variable part, by definition. Only a positive difference is written.

formula: host archetype capex (pooled) + median incremental capex of the set-aside examples
rationale: An incremental cost (the cost of adding a measure or retrofit to an existing plant) is not the archetype's own absolute cost. Adding the pooled cost of the host plant the measure is added to gives one, but the host value comes from other sources, plants and years than the increment, so the result is estimated, not sourced. Only where the archetype has no sourced value, the host is named in host-archetype.csv, and both are on the same unit. Not for CCS archetypes: a host plant with capture holds the host's cost (est-ccs-host-*) and a capture plant's incremental cost is its own cost (modeller 2026-10-02). Host costs are needed where a competition holds both the host and the host plus an add-on (modeller 2026-10-02).

formula: host archetype opex-fixed (pooled) + median incremental opex-fixed of the set-aside examples
rationale: An incremental cost (the cost of adding a measure or retrofit to an existing plant) is not the archetype's own absolute cost. Adding the pooled cost of the host plant the measure is added to gives one, but the host value comes from other sources, plants and years than the increment, so the result is estimated, not sourced. Only where the archetype has no sourced value, the host is named in host-archetype.csv, and both are on the same unit. Not for CCS archetypes: a host plant with capture holds the host's cost (est-ccs-host-*) and a capture plant's incremental cost is its own cost (modeller 2026-10-02). Host costs are needed where a competition holds both the host and the host plus an add-on (modeller 2026-10-02).

formula: host archetype capex (pooled), unchanged
rationale: A host plant with capture (an archetype with a _ccs- modifier outside the co2-capture family) differs in CIMS from its host only by a service request to the capture archetype, which carries the capture plant's cost. So it holds the host plant's cost, assumed the same with and without capture unless a source shows a significant difference (modeller 2026-10-02). Its own source rows are capture cost and are set aside (output/ccs-addon-cost.csv). Estimated, not identity: the assumption that capture leaves the host plant's cost unchanged is an approximation. Only where the host is named in host-archetype.csv. From 2026-10-10 only a fallback: the post-phase rule ccs-host-plus-addon-* overrides it wherever a capture add-on can be derived.

formula: host archetype opex-fixed (pooled), unchanged
rationale: A host plant with capture (an archetype with a _ccs- modifier outside the co2-capture family) differs in CIMS from its host only by a service request to the capture archetype, which carries the capture plant's cost. So it holds the host plant's cost, assumed the same with and without capture unless a source shows a significant difference (modeller 2026-10-02). Its own source rows are capture cost and are set aside (output/ccs-addon-cost.csv). Estimated, not identity: the assumption that capture leaves the host plant's cost unchanged is an approximation. Only where the host is named in host-archetype.csv. From 2026-10-10 only a fallback: the post-phase rule ccs-host-plus-addon-* overrides it wherever a capture add-on can be derived.

formula: host archetype opex-variable (pooled), unchanged
rationale: A host plant with capture (an archetype with a _ccs- modifier outside the co2-capture family) differs in CIMS from its host only by a service request to the capture archetype, which carries the capture plant's cost. So it holds the host plant's cost, assumed the same with and without capture unless a source shows a significant difference (modeller 2026-10-02). Its own source rows are capture cost and are set aside (output/ccs-addon-cost.csv). Estimated, not identity: the assumption that capture leaves the host plant's cost unchanged is an approximation. Only where the host is named in host-archetype.csv. From 2026-10-10 only a fallback: the post-phase rule ccs-host-plus-addon-* overrides it wherever a capture add-on can be derived.

formula: host archetype opex-total (pooled), unchanged
rationale: A host plant with capture (an archetype with a _ccs- modifier outside the co2-capture family) differs in CIMS from its host only by a service request to the capture archetype, which carries the capture plant's cost. So it holds the host plant's cost, assumed the same with and without capture unless a source shows a significant difference (modeller 2026-10-02). Its own source rows are capture cost and are set aside (output/ccs-addon-cost.csv). Estimated, not identity: the assumption that capture leaves the host plant's cost unchanged is an approximation. Only where the host is named in host-archetype.csv. OFF 2026-10-10: a host-with-capture variant is now the host plant plus the capture add-on (ccs-host-plus-addon-*); a copied host total or levelized cost would omit the add-on.

formula: host archetype cost-levelized (pooled), unchanged
rationale: A host plant with capture (an archetype with a _ccs- modifier outside the co2-capture family) differs in CIMS from its host only by a service request to the capture archetype, which carries the capture plant's cost. So it holds the host plant's cost, assumed the same with and without capture unless a source shows a significant difference (modeller 2026-10-02). Its own source rows are capture cost and are set aside (output/ccs-addon-cost.csv). Estimated, not identity: the assumption that capture leaves the host plant's cost unchanged is an approximation. Only where the host is named in host-archetype.csv. OFF 2026-10-10: a host-with-capture variant is now the host plant plus the capture add-on (ccs-host-plus-addon-*); a copied host total or levelized cost would omit the add-on.

formula: base archetype capex x median variant/base capex ratio from sources that price both a base and its variant with the same modifier, on the same equipment; an efficiency modifier's ratio is at least 1
inputs: capex of the base archetype; same-source variant/base pairs
rationale: ACTIVE (re-enabled; design.md). A variant (efficiency-strong, ccs-concentrated) differs from its base by a modifier whose cost effect sources can show directly: a source that prices both the base and the variant gives their ratio on the same basis, year and region. The median of at least two such ratios is applied to the base archetype's pooled value. Back-test 2026-10-01: 9 of 10 sourced variant capex values inside the range, 3 within 25%. ACTIVE 2026-10-09 (fill-methods proposal K1). NARROWED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check S142/RX014): pairs from the same equipment only, and efficiency-modifier pairs below 1 are dropped; ammonia reformers, tunnel kilns and boilers had priced a melting furnace's and an HVAC heater's efficient variants below their bases.

formula: host capex x (1 + median increment/host ratio of the same modifier)
inputs: capex of the base archetype; increment/host ratios from set-aside-host-cost.csv
rationale: A variant whose host has a capex but which has no priced measure of its own (so est-host-increment cannot run) takes the host cost plus the typical increment this database's own set-aside measure costs give for that modifier, as a share of the host cost: the median ratio of three or more archetypes, the range from the pool's quartiles (proposal K2).

formula: host's sourced fixed O&M x the variant's capex / the host's capex
inputs: host opex-fixed (sourced); variant capex; host capex
rationale: An efficiency variant is its host plus a measure, so its fixed O&M follows the host's own O&M-to-capex ratio rather than a pooled one. Before (to 2026-10-24) the pooled ratio could put a variant's fixed O&M at two-thirds of its host's while its capex was higher (coke dry quenching), so the variant's levelized cost fell below its host's. Only where the variant has no fixed O&M of its own and no set-aside increment (est-host-increment-opex-fixed runs first).

formula: base archetype opex-fixed x median variant/base opex-fixed ratio from sources that price both a base and its variant with the same modifier
inputs: opex-fixed of the base archetype; same-source variant/base pairs
rationale: PARKED 2026-10-01 (modeller): kept as a potential method to raise coverage, not applied. Set status to active to use it. A variant (efficiency-strong, ccs-concentrated) differs from its base by a modifier whose cost effect sources can show directly: a source that prices both the base and the variant gives their ratio on the same basis, year and region. The median of at least two such ratios is applied to the base archetype's pooled value. OFF 2026-10-01: it fills nothing (no variant lacking O&M has a base and two same-source pairs) and its back-test caught 2 of 5.

formula: capex per GJ-yr of heat output x the archetype's pooled energy use (GJ/t)
inputs: excluded capex rows per GJ-per-yr; specific-energy-consumption (class internal)
rationale: A capex a source gives per GJ-yr of heat output on a per-tonne archetype (the dryers, 2026-10-09) was excluded at normalise because the same example gives no GJ/t. Under the same-GJ condition of design s5 (same stream, side and scope) the archetype's own pooled energy use converts it; because that factor is pooled from other examples rather than the example's own, the result is graded estimated, not identity (ruling 2026-10-09, proposal K0).

formula: median lifetime of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; product unit need not match, 2026-10-09)
rationale: A service life is set by the equipment more than by the fuel it burns or the variant it is. Range spans the siblings' values and at least +/- the widen fraction of the central; output/fill-backtest.csv tests the rule on the cells that have a sourced value. Widen 0.25 chosen 2026-10-01 from the back-test: about 90% of sourced values fall inside (0.5 gave 97% with ranges twice as wide). EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): lighting_hid, lighting_led-controls take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life.

formula: median construction-time of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; product unit need not match, 2026-10-09)
rationale: Build time is set by the equipment and its scale more than by its carrier or variant. Range spans the siblings' values and at least +/- the widen fraction of the central; output/fill-backtest.csv tests the rule on the cells that have a sourced value. Widen 0.25 chosen 2026-10-01 from the back-test: about 90% of sourced values fall inside (0.5 gave 97% with ranges twice as wide).

formula: median capacity factor of the archetypes serving the same end use with the same product unit (sourced values; 3 or more)
inputs: capacity-factor of the archetypes on the same end use
rationale: How much of the year a unit runs is set by the duty it serves: a pump, dehydrator or turboexpander in a gas plant runs at the gas plant's availability, not at the median of other rotating machines or of a let-down turbine that runs on spare pressure (sanity-check 2026-10-11, OG013). So the end use's median comes before the equipment siblings and the equipment class. EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): turboexpander_ngl-recovery, adsorber_molecular-sieve, pump_electric-station, pump_plunger-lift, pump_artificial-lift, drilling-rig_diesel, drilling-rig_electric, drilling-rig_battery-hybrid, fracturing-fleet_electric take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life. Not on the electrolysis cells or the off-road mobile equipment and diesel and dual-fuel frac fleets, which carry judgements (sanity-check 2026-10-23, S137).

A methane control's capacity is the methane it avoids in a year, as its sources state it (methane avoided per installation per year: IEA 2026 reduction volumes, US EPA Natural Gas STAR), and its capex is per that same annual tonnage. The annual output is then that tonnage and the levelized cost needs no further capacity factor, so the factor is 100% by definition. Before (to 2026-10-24) a sibling or class-median factor (46-85%) lowered the annual output below the sourced tonnage and raised the levelized cost by the same factor.

formula: median capacity-factor of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; product unit need not match, 2026-10-09)
rationale: How much of the year equipment runs is set mostly by the duty it serves, which siblings share. Range spans the siblings' values and at least +/- the widen fraction of the central; output/fill-backtest.csv tests the rule on the cells that have a sourced value. Widen 0.25 chosen 2026-10-01 from the back-test: about 90% of sourced values fall inside (0.5 gave 97% with ranges twice as wide). EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): turboexpander_ngl-recovery take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life. Not on the electrolysis cells or the off-road mobile equipment and diesel and dual-fuel frac fleets, which carry judgements (sanity-check 2026-10-23, S137).

formula: median sourced capacity factor of the archetypes in the same equipment class (records/fill/equipment-class.csv), else of all archetypes
rationale: The levelized cost needs a capacity factor on every archetype. How much of the year equipment runs is set by the kind of duty (continuous process plant, batch heat equipment, mobile equipment), so the class median stands in where no sibling has one, else the median of all archetypes. EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): turboexpander_ngl-recovery, adsorber_molecular-sieve, pump_electric-station, pump_plunger-lift, pump_artificial-lift, drilling-rig_diesel, drilling-rig_electric, drilling-rig_battery-hybrid, fracturing-fleet_electric take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life. Not on the electrolysis cells or the off-road mobile equipment and diesel and dual-fuel frac fleets, which carry judgements (sanity-check 2026-10-23, S137). Not on the two solar concentrators (2026-10-24, sanity-check run, S102): the heat-supply class median (86%) is a fired plant's hours, and a solar field's factor is drafted from solar-collector's sourced 22.8% instead.
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: median sourced lifetime of the archetypes in the same equipment class (records/fill/equipment-class.csv)
rationale: A wider sibling rule for archetypes with no sibling at all: service life is set by the kind of equipment (process plant, heat equipment, rotating machinery, mobile equipment, wells), so the class median stands in, with the class span and at least +/-25% as the range (proposal L1). Back-tested like the sibling rules. EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): lighting_hid, lighting_led-controls take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life.

formula: value
rationale: Where neither a sibling nor three class members carry a sourced lifetime, a published engineering life for the equipment class, from a registered reference named in fill-assumption.csv (proposal L2).

formula: annual output = capacity x capacity factor x hours (MW x 31,536 GJ/yr; kt/yr x 1000); the better-supported size anchors
rationale: Capacity, capacity factor and annual output are pooled from different examples, so they can disagree (2026-10-28 check: 16 archetypes off by more than 2x, the boilers by 9-32x). Where they differ by more than 10%, one size anchors and the other is recalculated: the annual output when facility statistics (Petrinex, AER, BCER) give it, as the median of existing plants (Brad 2026-10-21); otherwise the value with the better grade, then more examples, capacity on a tie. A sourced value that is recalculated moves to target as-sourced. Grade is the worst of identity and the inputs.

formula: capacity x capacity-factor x hours (MW x 8760 h x 3.6 GJ/MWh; kt/yr x 1000)
rationale: A unit's yearly output is its rated capacity run at its capacity factor, by definition; the capacity factor may be an estimated (sibling) value, and the result then inherits that grade (proposal O1).

formula: median annual output of the archetypes serving the same end use with the same product unit (sourced values and capacity x capacity-factor identities; 3 or more)
inputs: annual-output of the archetypes on the same end use
rationale: The archetypes competing on one end use serve plants of about the same size (a kiln and its alternatives make the same clinker plant's output), so the end use's median output stands in where the archetype has no sibling; range the pool's span and at least +/-50% (proposal O3, fitted on this database rather than a proxy table). Runs before the sibling rule since 2026-10-09 (back-test 9 of 9 inside the range against 3 of 15 for siblings). Pool of one or more from 2026-10-09: the archetypes on one end use serve the same plant, so even one sized archetype says what scale the end use runs at. Range x3 either side of the central (multiplicative).

formula: median annual output of the nearest siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; same product unit)
rationale: Plant scale is set by the process and the product, not by the carrier or the variant: a variant of a kiln serves the same plant as the kiln. The nearest siblings' median stands in, with their span and at least +/-50% as the range, since plant sizes vary widely (proposal O2). Back-test 2026-10-09: 3 of 15 sourced outputs inside a +/-50% range, so the range is widened to +/-100% and the end-use median runs first (9 of 9 inside); plant sizes within an equipment term vary several-fold, and the value is a scale, not a cost the model competes on. Restricted 2026-10-09 to tier 1 (same equipment and discriminator): a ceramic kiln took a cement kiln's 1.6 Mt/yr at tier 2. Range x3 either side of the central.

formula: value
rationale: A typical Canadian unit size per end use or equipment class from a registered benchmark reference (proposal O3). Costs are per unit of annual capacity, so the size sets the number of units in the stock, not the cost the model competes on. OFF 2026-10-09: no benchmark reference registered yet; the end-use median (est-end-use-annual-output) and judgements stand in. Set active once fill-assumption.csv holds a plant-size group.

formula: base archetype energy use x (1 - saving); saving = the variant's sourced emissions-reduction-potential, else the bucket definition (fill-assumption.csv, proxy); capped so the variant's efficiency stays at or below the equipment's maximum
inputs: group=bucket-saving; specific-energy-consumption of the base archetype; emissions-reduction-potential
rationale: The UKERC stage (pipeline/ukerc_saving.py) already derives a variant's energy use from its base and the members' savings. The same relation for variants whose saving comes from another source: the variant's own emissions-reduction-potential, on the stated assumption that for a same-fuel measure the emission saving equals the energy saving; otherwise the bucket's own definition (moderate up to about 15%, strong more), as a proxy constant. The total and every carrier of the base are scaled alike, so the split still sums (proposal E3). CAPPED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check S142/HPCH006, RX005): on a GJ-output archetype whose base has an efficiency of 100% or less, the saving stops where the variant's efficiency would reach the equipment's maximum (motors and drives 97%, pumps, fans and compressors 92%, others 97%; EFF_MAX in pipeline/fill.py).

formula: 100 / specific-energy-consumption
rationale: An efficiency variant whose energy use comes from its base and a saving (est-bucket-saving-sec) takes its efficiency from that energy use, so the two agree; before, est-sibling-efficiency gave it the base's efficiency unchanged beside a lower energy use (sanity-check 2026-10-23, S142/HPCH006, RX005). Runs after the bucket saving and before the sibling efficiency.

formula: median efficiency of the nearest non-CHP siblings with a sourced value (same equipment and discriminator, else same equipment; same product unit); a capture or efficiency variant takes its host's efficiency first, with its extra energy use added to the input; siblings must share the product
rationale: On energy-service archetypes the efficiency is set by the equipment class far more than by the carrier or the variant, so a dryer, direct heater, engine or fan takes its siblings' median; range their span and at least +/-15% of the central (about 10 points). Costs are not copied between siblings; efficiency is the one quantity that is nearly invariant across them. Never from a CHP sibling to a heat-only one, and never for per-tonne process archetypes, where a route change is the reason they are separate (proposal E4). id-sec-from-efficiency then gives the energy use. Not on the two small nuclear reactors: their siblings under `reactor` are chemical reactors (63% from gas-to-liquids and hydrotreating), which says nothing about a fission reactor (2026-10-13). EXCLUDED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check OG013, OT006, OT008): mobile-equipment_diesel-electric, mobile-equipment_spark-ignition, mobile-equipment_hydrogen-combustion take a drafted judgement instead, because the analogue this rule picks is the wrong duty or life. CHANGED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check S142/HPCH005, PB009): siblings must make the same product (a heat well does not take a power plant's efficiency); a variant takes its host's efficiency, adjusted for its extra energy use, ahead of the siblings. Not on reactor_co2-to-fischer-tropsch (2026-10-24, sanity-check run batch F): its siblings are biofuel upgrading units (hydrotreating, HTL, alcohol-to-jet) at 60-94%, while its own energy use (1.78 GJ of electricity per GJ, electrolysis included) gives 56%; a judgement carries that.

formula: value
rationale: Machine-drive archetypes distinguished by motor efficiency class take the class band of the standard that defines them (IEC 60034-30-1 / NEMA Premium), registered as a reference (proposal E6). OFF 2026-10-09: every motor archetype carries a sourced efficiency (NEMA Premium sits on motor_induction-standard, ruling 2026-10-07), so there is nothing to fill; kept for the record.

formula: capex x median opex-fixed/capex of archetypes with both sourced (same equipment, else family, else all; pools of 5 or more)
rationale: ACTIVE (re-enabled; design.md). Fixed O&M is commonly stated as a share of capital cost per year; the share is taken from archetypes in this database with both values sourced, nearest pool of at least five first. Range: the smallest to largest share in that pool. Back-test 2026-10-01 (87 archetypes with both sourced): 71 inside the range, but only 24 centrals within 25% (typical error a factor of 1.7). The shares spread from under 1% to over 12% a year, so treat these as placeholders for the sanity-check pass. Pools of 3 with the 10-90th percentile caught only 50. ACTIVE 2026-10-09 (proposal F1), re-tuned: the pool shares the archetype's product unit (a share per tonne and a share per GJ behave differently), the nearest pool needs 3 archetypes (same equipment) or 5 (family, then all), and the range is the pool's interquartile span rather than its extremes. The capex it scales may itself be a fill; the result inherits that grade. A fourth pool level (2026-10-09) takes archetypes of any product unit, since the ratio is per year of the same unit on both sides; it is reached only where the m3 and m archetypes have no pool of their own. NARROWED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check S142/OG001, OG002): abatement devices (product t of methane or CO2 abated) and product plants never share a ratio pool; the same-equipment pool needs 5 archetypes, like the others. POOL-AS-PLANT 2026-10-28 (Brad, OG002): flare-gas recovery is a compressor station priced like a plant, so it takes its ratio from the non-abating plants at any product unit, not from the methane devices (which had put its O&M at 18% of capex).

formula: share-of:capex
rationale: Where no pool of archetypes with both capex and fixed O&M reaches the minimum, fixed O&M is the published convention for the equipment class as a share of capex per year, from a registered reference named in fill-assumption.csv (proposal F2). The capex may itself be a fill; the result inherits that grade.

formula: capex x median opex-variable/capex of archetypes with both sourced (same equipment, else family, else all; same product unit; material classes only)
rationale: For equipment classes whose variable non-fuel O&M is a real cost (consumables, reagents, catalysts, refractory, tyres: records/fill/equipment-class.csv vom-class material), the variable cost per unit of product is scaled from capex with the ratio archetypes of the same class show; range the pool's interquartile span. A weak fit that stands in until a source or a judgement replaces it (proposal V4). The capex may itself be a fill; the result inherits that grade. A fourth pool level (2026-10-09) takes archetypes of any product unit, since the ratio is per year of the same unit on both sides; it is reached only where the m3 and m archetypes have no pool of their own. NARROWED 2026-10-24 (sanity-check S142/OG001, OG002): abatement devices (product t of methane or CO2 abated) and product plants never share a ratio pool; the same-equipment pool needs 5 archetypes, like the others.

formula: variable O&M is real but small for this equipment class and is folded into fixed O&M (records/fill/equipment-class.csv vom-class minor)
rationale: Boilers, heaters, dryers, CHP, motors, pumps, fans, compressors, space conditioning and lighting have a variable non-fuel O&M that is small against fixed O&M and fuel. CIMS carries a variable O&M field, but a guessed small number would add a red-graded value the model would not distinguish from zero; the cost is carried in fixed O&M instead (ruling 2026-10-04, proposal V3).

formula: no meaningful variable O&M for this equipment class (records/fill/equipment-class.csv vom-class none)
rationale: Programmes, controls, seals, flares, pipeline liners and storage have no variable non-fuel operating cost worth representing (proposal V3).

formula: capacity-factor does not characterise a do-nothing option (no equipment)
rationale: A no-abatement option has no equipment, so it has no size, output or build time; costs, energy, emissions reduction and lifetime are judgements (records/fill/fill-judgement.csv).

formula: annual-output does not characterise a do-nothing option (no equipment)
rationale: A no-abatement option has no equipment, so it has no size, output or build time; costs, energy, emissions reduction and lifetime are judgements (records/fill/fill-judgement.csv).

formula: capacity does not characterise a do-nothing option (no equipment)
rationale: A no-abatement option has no equipment, so it has no size, output or build time; costs, energy, emissions reduction and lifetime are judgements (records/fill/fill-judgement.csv).

formula: construction-time does not characterise a do-nothing option (no equipment)
rationale: A no-abatement option has no equipment, so it has no size, output or build time; costs, energy, emissions reduction and lifetime are judgements (records/fill/fill-judgement.csv).

formula: a methane control whose CIMS service request is in t CH4 or m3 of gas: its own energy use is negligible or is the gas it saves
rationale: The methane-control archetypes on the venting, fugitive and flaring nodes are characterised by the methane they abate, not by an energy use; the device's own energy use is negligible (a low-bleed pneumatic, a seal, a leak survey) or is the gas it recovers. Controls that do draw power (vapour-recovery and instrument-air compressors, electric-drive compressors, pumps) are excluded from the marker and take a value by another rule or a judgement (proposal E5).

formula: the characterising quantity is a capacity factor, a round-trip efficiency, a transport loss or an abatement rate, not an energy use per unit of output
rationale: Wind, solar, geothermal and storage archetypes, hydrogen pipelines and caverns, flares, leak-detection programmes and pneumatic devices are not characterised by an energy use per unit of product: a capacity factor, a round-trip efficiency, a loss rate or an abatement rate is what the model needs, and those stay where they are (proposal E7).

inputs: the species rows of the same emissions parameter
rationale: The CO2-eq on an archetype is the sum of its species at AR5 GWPs (Brad 2026-10-28). Where a CO2-eq pooled from other examples disagrees with the species by more than 2%, the species sum replaces it and the pooled CO2-eq moves to target as-sourced. Runs before the variant and capture rules, so a capture variant works from its host's consistent figure.

formula: the host archetype's annual output (records/fill/host-archetype.csv)
rationale: A variant is its host plant plus an efficiency measure or a capture plant, so it has the host's size (ruling 2026-10-10: archetypes and their variants consistent and logical). Overrides what the variant had; a value the variant's own sources give is kept as target as-sourced (a secondary parameter).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: annual output / capacity factor (/ 1000 for kt/yr; / 8760 h / 3.6 GJ/MWh for MW)
rationale: Where the annual output is the median of existing facilities (regulator statistics), the capacity follows from it, so capacity x capacity factor = output (Brad 2026-10-21). The licensed, design or large-plant capacity the sources give moves to target as-sourced. Grade is the worst of identity and the inputs.

formula: annual output / capacity x 100
rationale: Gas plants: the capacity is the Alberta licensed capacity (AER ST50A) and the output the median throughput of the same plants (Petrinex), so the capacity factor follows from them and the three stay consistent (Brad 2026-10-21). Alberta plants run well below licence.

formula: capacity = annual output / capacity factor (/ 1000 for kt/yr; / 31,536 GJ/yr per MW)
rationale: An archetype with an annual output and a capacity factor but no capacity takes capacity = output / capacity factor, so the three agree (Brad 2026-10-28: fill the missing capacities). Grade is the worst of identity and the inputs, so a guessed output gives a guessed capacity. Runs after every annual output is filled and before the variant size rules.

formula: central electrolysis capex x 1.37 (same-source 20 vs 100 MW and 10 vs 100 MW ratios, 1.32-1.53)
rationale: On-site electrolysis (about 1-20 MW) costs more per unit than a central plant (about 100 MW-1 GW) because balance of plant, installation and staffing do not scale down. Pooled across sources the costs run the other way (recent real-project costs sit in the central pool, older and future-year estimates in the on-site pool), so the size effect comes from sources that price both sizes: Lazard 2021 20 vs 100 MW (alkaline 1.36-1.39, PEM 1.32-1.33 across its three efficiency cases) and DEA 2026 10 vs 100 MW (AEC 1.53, PEM 1.45) for capex; DEA 10 vs 100 MW for fixed O&M (AEC 1.68, PEM 1.60). The pooled on-site value moves to target as-sourced.

formula: central electrolysis fixed O&M x 1.64 (DEA 10 vs 100 MW, 1.60-1.68)
rationale: On-site electrolysis (about 1-20 MW) costs more per unit than a central plant (about 100 MW-1 GW) because balance of plant, installation and staffing do not scale down. Pooled across sources the costs run the other way (recent real-project costs sit in the central pool, older and future-year estimates in the on-site pool), so the size effect comes from sources that price both sizes: Lazard 2021 20 vs 100 MW (alkaline 1.36-1.39, PEM 1.32-1.33 across its three efficiency cases) and DEA 2026 10 vs 100 MW (AEC 1.53, PEM 1.45) for capex; DEA 10 vs 100 MW for fixed O&M (AEC 1.68, PEM 1.60). The pooled on-site value moves to target as-sourced.

formula: the host archetype's capacity
rationale: A variant is its host plant plus an efficiency measure or a capture plant, so it has the host's size (ruling 2026-10-10: archetypes and their variants consistent and logical). Overrides what the variant had; a value the variant's own sources give is kept as target as-sourced (a secondary parameter).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: the host archetype's capacity factor
rationale: A variant is its host plant plus an efficiency measure or a capture plant, so it has the host's size (ruling 2026-10-10: archetypes and their variants consistent and logical). Overrides what the variant had; a value the variant's own sources give is kept as target as-sourced (a secondary parameter).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: fixed O&M + rebuild cost / campaign length / annual capacity (records/reference/rebuild-allowance.csv)
rationale: The asset life (25 years for glass furnaces, Gielen 1997) spans more than one furnace campaign; the cold repair at the end of each campaign is a cost the plant bears within that life, so it is carried as fixed O&M rather than a shorter lifetime (user 2026-10-15). The allowance is kept as target rebuild.
decided: user 2026-10-15 (glass furnaces: 25-year asset life with the rebuild cost as O&M)

formula: host plant capex + capture add-on capex per unit of the host's annual capacity
inputs: capex of the host; output/ccs-addon-cost.csv; capex of the capture archetypes on the CCS node; CO2 captured per unit of product
rationale: A host-with-capture variant is the host plant plus the capture add-on (ruling 2026-10-10). The add-on: same-source evidence first (the source's incremental capture cost on this variant, else its plant with capture less its plant without: output/ccs-addon-cost.csv rows); else the median of the capture archetypes on the matching CCS node (diffuse or concentrated) per t CO2 x the CO2 captured per unit of the host's product (the variant's emissions-captured, else the host's CO2 x share-to-capture x a 90% capture rate). The parts are kept as targets host-plant and ccs-add-on; the CIMS export writes the host-plant part plus the service request to the CCS node, which carries the capture cost there. On the diffuse (post-combustion) node the tier-2 add-on is the reference standard amine plant, capture-unit_amine, not the node median (user 2026-10-23).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: host plant fixed O&M + capture add-on fixed O&M
rationale: A host-with-capture variant is the host plant plus the capture add-on (ruling 2026-10-10). The add-on: same-source evidence first (the source's incremental capture cost on this variant, else its plant with capture less its plant without: output/ccs-addon-cost.csv rows); else the median of the capture archetypes on the matching CCS node (diffuse or concentrated) per t CO2 x the CO2 captured per unit of the host's product (the variant's emissions-captured, else the host's CO2 x share-to-capture x a 90% capture rate). The parts are kept as targets host-plant and ccs-add-on; the CIMS export writes the host-plant part plus the service request to the CCS node, which carries the capture cost there. On the diffuse (post-combustion) node the tier-2 add-on is the reference standard amine plant, capture-unit_amine, not the node median (user 2026-10-23).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: host plant variable O&M (0 where not applicable) + capture add-on variable O&M (solvent make-up and the like) per unit of product
rationale: A host-with-capture variant is the host plant plus the capture add-on (ruling 2026-10-10). The add-on: same-source evidence first (the source's incremental capture cost on this variant, else its plant with capture less its plant without: output/ccs-addon-cost.csv rows); else the median of the capture archetypes on the matching CCS node (diffuse or concentrated) per t CO2 x the CO2 captured per unit of the host's product (the variant's emissions-captured, else the host's CO2 x share-to-capture x a 90% capture rate). The parts are kept as targets host-plant and ccs-add-on; the CIMS export writes the host-plant part plus the service request to the CCS node, which carries the capture cost there. On the diffuse (post-combustion) node the tier-2 add-on is the reference standard amine plant, capture-unit_amine, not the node median (user 2026-10-23).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: host energy use (every carrier) + the capture plant's: the CCS node's median GJ per t CO2, split by the node archetypes' mean carrier shares, x the CO2 captured per unit of product
inputs: specific-energy-consumption of the host and of the capture archetypes on the node; CO2 captured per unit of product
rationale: The capture plant's reboiler steam and compression electricity belong to the variant as much as its cost does (ruling 2026-10-10). Taken from the capture archetypes rather than the energy rows sources give on hosts with capture (output/ccs-addon-energy.csv), which often mix host and capture energy. Parts kept as targets host-plant and ccs-add-on. On the diffuse (post-combustion) node the tier-2 add-on is the reference standard amine plant, capture-unit_amine, not the node median (user 2026-10-23).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: the host's combustion and process emissions (gross, every species); emissions-captured = capture rate x share-to-capture x the host's gross CO2; emissions-total = the host's gross total less emissions-captured (net of capture)
inputs: emissions of the host; CO2 captured per unit of product
rationale: The variant is the host plant, so it emits what the host emits; the captured CO2 is removed in CIMS through the CCS node (emissions_removal = capture rate x the host's service request, cims/to-fix.md #4). Net emissions are total less captured. A variant's own sourced emissions (often already net) are kept as target as-sourced. CHANGED 2026-10-13 (ruling on sanity-check section 4.3): emissions-total on a capture variant is NET of capture; emissions-total + emissions-captured = the host gross. Combustion and process stay gross. CHANGED 2026-10-24 (user, sanity-check S138): captured is always capture rate x share-to-capture x the host's gross CO2 (emissions-total, else combustion plus process), with share and rate from pipeline/capture_share.py; a sourced captured tonnage moves to as-sourced, because it may come from another plant (61% capture on lime, zero net where it exceeded the host's gross).
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost); modeller 2026-10-13

formula: judged thermal efficiency (process-heat-efficiency.csv); a variant: host efficiency x host energy use / own energy use
rationale: Light-industrial heat archetypes (dryers, ovens, kilns, heat exchangers, cleaning systems, presses, melting and heat-treatment furnaces) compete on process-heat sub-nodes measured in GJ of process heat (ruling E2), so their thermal efficiency matters; the judged figures already used for the per-GJ-of-heat bands now also fill the efficiency column (Brad 2026-10-28). Judged values are graded guess; variant values are identities on the host's process heat per t.

inputs: the species rows of the same emissions parameter
rationale: As id-co2e-consistency, run again after the capture rules so a capture variant's net CO2-eq also sums its species (Brad 2026-10-28).

formula: (capex x capital recovery factor + fixed O&M) / capacity factor + variable O&M, at the reference discount rate (fill-assumption discount-rate) and the archetype lifetime; energy excluded
inputs: capex; opex-fixed; opex-variable (0 where not applicable); lifetime; capacity-factor; discount rate
rationale: A calculated levelized cost on every archetype, to compare options on one basis (ruling 2026-10-10). Costs are per unit of nameplate annual capacity (2026-10-10), so dividing by the capacity factor gives the cost per unit actually made. Energy is excluded: the database does not price fuels. Takes the worst grade of its inputs; the discount rate is a stated convention. A levelized cost a source prints stays in the column with no target, for comparison. BAND CHANGED 2026-10-13 (sanity-check S119): low and high are the cost band (capex and O&M low and high) at the central lifetime and capacity factor, not every input at its worst corner.
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost); modeller 2026-10-13

formula: cost-levelized calculated + energy use by carrier x reference 2025 price (records/reference/energy-price.csv)
inputs: cost-levelized calculated; specific-energy-consumption by carrier; energy-price.csv
rationale: Without energy an electric option looks cheap beside a fired one for the wrong reason. Each carrier is priced at a reference 2025 Canadian industrial price; steam and heat at the fuel-fired boiler's own levelized cost and hydrogen at the methane reformer's (derived); by-product gases, black liquor and waste heat are internal (0). Written only where every carrier the archetype uses has a price.
decided: modeller 2026-10-10 (variants consistent with hosts; levelized cost)

formula: sum over biogenic carriers of specific-energy-consumption(carrier) x biogenic CO2 emission factor(carrier)
rationale: Biomass burned times its carbon content, written as emissions-biomass (CIMS), apart from fossil CO2: solid, liquid and gaseous biomass alike. Kept off archetypes whose biomass is a feedstock (its carbon leaves in the fuel or product made) and off capture variants, whose biogenic CO2 is the host's net of capture.
